agentHost: update client tools without restarting sessions

Update Copilot client tools in place when session initialization data stays the same.

- Replace client tool definitions and handlers through the SDK setTools API.
- Compare applied initialization data before a live update or required restart.
- Keep customization scopes stable across turns and client tool changes.
- Compare discovered resource URIs without their mutable serialization caches.
- Add restart diagnostics and tests for tool updates, routing, and scope isolation.
- Use a short-lived Set to track ancestors during stable serialization.

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

### Reviewer notes

Tool-only additions, replacements, removals, and renames use `setTools`, including during active turns. Applied definitions and routing commit only after SDK success. Shell, server, extension, Computer Use, and MCP routing tools remain registered.

Changes to the resolved initialization payload still require a restart. In particular, toggling Integrated Browser changes tool-gated system-prompt guidance and therefore still restarts; this PR does not change that guidance.

Workspace-scoped plugin URIs are preserved. The scope fix aligns the chat handler with the Sessions provider for workspaceless sessions and host-declared scratch folders, without changing sensitive-edit roots.

### Validation

Merged the fetched `origin/main` and resolved one overlapping test import while retaining both additions. Refreshed dependencies with the repository-required Node 24.22.1.

- `fnm exec --using 24.22.1 npm run typecheck-client` — passed after the merge.
- Existing **Build Fast** task (`npm run build-fast`) — passed after the merge.
- `fnm exec --using 24.22.1 ./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotPluginConverters.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatContribution.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostCustomizationService.test.ts` — 3,454 passed, one pending.
- `npm run -s precommit` — repository commit hooks passed for both commits, including merge hygiene.
- Changed-TypeScript targeted ESLint and `git diff --cached --check` — passed before the merge.
- Manual Code OSS log verification before the merge: disabling two ordinary tools reduced the client catalog from 20 to 18, the runtime emitted `session.tools_updated`, and the next turn completed without SDK shutdown, resume, or error.

Full integration and smoke suites were not run. The live scenario was not repeated after merging main.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous call path and per-send frequency are explicit, and the resolver's YAML parse/allocation work is directly traced. Exact milliseconds and prevalence of large prompt overrides are uncertain, so severity is low.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and temporary objects from tool filtering/sorting, prompt construction, YAML parsing, custom-agent projection, and deep comparison
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The synchronous cost is paid once for every send/resume even when nothing changed, and grows with the client-tool count, custom-agent/tool-reference count, and prompt-override YAML size.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased turn-start latency and CPU/GC pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, the common per-turn refresh path compared client tool definitions structurally; prompt overrides and the launch-only SDK configuration were resolved only while creating or resuming a session.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added tail check invokes clientToolsRequireRestart for every otherwise-current session. That calls configuration.resolve(tools), which reconstructs the complete tool-dependent launch payload; when a prompt override is configured, applyPromptOverridesFromString reparses the retained YAML on every invocation before the result is deeply compared.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 7159 appends `entry.clientToolsRequireRestart(currentSnapshot.tools)` to every otherwise-clean refresh check; this per-turn call did not exist before the PR.
Findings.Title: Cache launch-only tool configuration between changes
Findings.Impact: Every message waits synchronously for this reconstruction before it can be sent. The overhead is most visible in sessions with large experimental prompt overrides, many enabled tools, or many custom agents, and repeats across long conversations despite unchanged inputs.
Findings.Evidence: _sendMessageOnce and _resumeTurnOnce await _refreshSessionConfiguration on the turn critical path. The new line 7159 unconditionally calls clientToolsRequireRestart on the common no-restart path; copilotAgentSession.ts:3674 resolves the full configuration, and copilotSessionLauncher.ts:1451/1461 reparses promptOverride.content and rebuilds filtered names, systemMessage, excludedTools, mapped custom agents, and sorted built-in-agent tool lists. The new test at copilotAgent.test.ts:27358 explicitly demonstrates that this comparison runs on each of three consecutive sends, including equal configurations.
Findings.Recommendation: Retain the last resolved launch-only payload and recompute it only when tool definitions or the relevant configuration settings change. At minimum, parse the launch-frozen prompt override once and reuse its parsed representation while still re-evaluating settings that are intentionally live.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The old restart comparison used generic deep equality on discovered resources, so URI objects whose mutable fsPath/toString caches differed after launch were treated as customization changes and caused an unnecessary SDK-session teardown/resume.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Unchanged discovered agents or additional-root instructions could restart the SDK at subsequent turn boundaries, adding avoidable session-resume latency; the new integration test exercises repeated turns/tool toggles and expects one launch with no refreshes.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The PR compares discovered resources with semantic URI equality while comparing the remaining metadata structurally, preventing cache-only URI mutations from triggering session restarts.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The deleted base lines compared discoveredAgents/additionalRootInstructions with generic equals. Added discoveredResourceEquals strips uri and uses isEqual for it. Tests populate URI fsPath/toString caches and verify no restart, and the multi-turn integration test records a single create, zero disconnects, and zero configuration refreshes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Sending or resuming a turn in an existing Copilot Agent Host chat with unchanged tools and customizations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before the SDK send/resume can begin, the queued refresh reads the stored working directory, obtains the current customization snapshot, compares restart state, and now synchronously resolves and deeply compares the complete tool-dependent launch payload. The newly reported resolver work is directly on this critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the persisted working directory/session metadata used by refresh validation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same persisted-directory read was already performed on every operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the turn can proceed

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Await customization synchronization/discovery when the anchor is not already settled
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one snapshot/discovery pass per refresh anchor; settled state and shared anchors avoid per-resource reads on the common warm path
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same snapshot/discovery path existed before the PR.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One execution per send/resume; CPU and allocation scale with enabled client tools, custom agents and their tool references, and retained prompt-override YAML bytes. Effective cardinality is one payload rebuild per turn, not per tool.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-chat turn work is serialized by the chat queue; there is no parallelism or coalescing across successive turns. Snapshot subwork overlaps the stored-directory read, but the new resolver executes synchronously afterward.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Customization anchors and discovery state are shared/cached, while the launch-frozen prompt-override content is retained. The PR does not cache its parsed form or the resolved launch payload, so equal warm-state turns repeat that work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added call is unconditional on the common otherwise-clean turn path, and its transitive YAML parse, projections, sorting, allocations, and deep comparison are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact added milliseconds depend on tool/custom-agent counts and prompt-override size; large overrides are an experimental configuration, so prevalence is uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity repeated work because launch-only configuration is rebuilt on every turn despite unchanged inputs.

Scenarios.Scenario: Applying an actual client-tool addition, removal, rename, or preferred-client schema change to a live or active session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: At the queued send/resume/configuration boundary, initialization data is resolved, client SDK Tool objects and MCP routing proxies are built, and the complete tool catalog is sent through session.setTools before the turn proceeds. If launch-only data changes, the existing restart path is used instead.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Replace the SDK session's full tool catalog with session.setTools
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One awaited call per accepted effective tool-snapshot change; identical/order-only snapshots are suppressed
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A structural tool change caused SDK session teardown and create/resume rather than an in-place setTools call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the triggering send/resume boundary until the SDK accepts the catalog

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query runtime built-in tool descriptors when an executionSubagent client tool may conflict
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once at launch and on later replacements only until runtime execution-subagent availability is positively cached; zero when the client tool is absent
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The descriptor query already ran during each session launch; tool changes previously forced a new launch and therefore another query.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Disconnect and create/resume the SDK session when tool-dependent systemMessage, toolSearch, excludedTools, or customAgents changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One restart only for an effective launch-only payload change
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every structural client-tool change took this restart path, including changes that did not alter launch-only data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the turn and is substantially more expensive than setTools

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One full replacement per effective merged tool snapshot change at a queued boundary; payload construction and serialization scale with deduplicated tool count plus MCP routing proxies, not with all contributing clients independently.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-chat configuration work is serialized. setTools is awaited, so replacements do not burst concurrently within one chat; separate live chats can update independently with no new global limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Applied definitions suppress identical replacements. Positive runtime execution-subagent availability is cached per CopilotSession in a WeakSet; negative availability is not cached, but each changed snapshot previously required a full restart/catalog check, so this does not amplify the pre-diff boundary count for the same effective updates.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: tests record one initial create, in-place updates, no disconnect, retry semantics, and full-catalog preservation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK setTools latency and cross-chat aggregate update frequency are not measured, but it replaces a heavier restart for the same trigger.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression beyond the separately reported per-turn resolver work; the boundary change reduces latency and process/IPC work relative to restarting sessions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Claiming a prewarmed provisional session after tools change before the first send
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The first send checks launch staleness. Launch-only tool projection changes discard the warm runtime; otherwise updateClientTools is awaited and the same runtime is materialized and used.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Replace tools on the prewarmed SDK session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for identical tools; one call when the effective tool snapshot changed compatibly
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Any client-tool change discarded/deleted the warm session and created a cold SDK session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the first send can claim and materialize the warm runtime

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Delete/disconnect the stale warm SDK session and create a replacement when launch-only data changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One only for launch-only projection changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All tool changes used this cold-start path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One comparison per claimed warm draft and at most one setTools replacement for the effective tool snapshot.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Warm launch and first send share the chat queue, so claiming, replacement, and disposal cannot interleave.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The warm session retains its applied snapshot. Identical tools return before SDK Tool construction or IPC; a changed compatible snapshot commits only after setTools succeeds.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed tests explicitly show one create and one setTools for compatible changes versus the former two creates and deletion.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact first-send savings depend on SDK startup duration and prewarm adoption rate.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refreshing unchanged discovered agents/instructions whose URI serialization caches were populated during launch
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each turn compares ordered discovered resources before deciding whether to restart the SDK. The new comparator uses semantic URI equality and structural metadata equality entirely in process.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: SDK disconnect/resume that generic deep URI equality could falsely trigger
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Now zero for cache-only URI differences; one for a real ordered resource/metadata change
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Generic deep equality could interpret launch-populated URI caches as customization changes and restart the SDK.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A false positive previously blocked the next turn on a session restart

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Linear in discovered agent plus additional-root-instruction count per refresh; shallow rest-object allocations occur per compared resource.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Runs synchronously inside the serialized per-chat refresh.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Mutable URI fsPath/toString caches are ignored, preventing cache-state differences from invalidating the session. Discovery remains shared by customization anchors.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the comparator and tests directly establish the false-restart mechanism and its removal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The frequency of cache divergence depends on which URI accessors launch paths touch, but dedicated tests reproduce fsPath and toString variants.
Scenarios.Verdict: Performance regression fix recorded with the blamed introducing commit; no review finding against this PR.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolving workbench customization scopes and sensitive-edit roots for workspaceless or scratch-folder sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session hydration computes customization roots from in-memory session metadata and resource URI mappings; sensitive-edit configuration deliberately continues to use all working-directory roots. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is introduced by the changed helper split.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Filtering is O(W*S) for working-directory and declared-scratch-folder counts, which are realistically small workspace-root collections.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous local computation during session content provisioning; no queue or burst behavior changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses hydrated session state and configuration-service values; there is no new cache or retained collection.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High after tracing both helper callers and tests for local/remote quick chats.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Workspace root counts vary, but typical cardinality is single digits and no expensive boundary is crossed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stable serialization for cache keys, database payloads, automation state, and MCP routing hashes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: stableStringify recursively sorts keys and now uses a short-lived strong Set for current ancestors, deleting each object after its subtree is serialized.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Deterministically serialize object graphs for keys/payload comparisons
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One traversal per existing call site, unchanged by the PR
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same traversal and ancestor add/delete behavior used a WeakSet.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Depends on the existing caller; the diff changes only cycle-tracking container semantics

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Time remains proportional to object graph serialization plus key sorting; retained ancestor objects are bounded by recursion depth and released when the call returns.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each serialization call is synchronous and independent; no changed coalescing or concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No persistent cache is added. Shared sibling references serialize in full because entries are removed after traversal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the complete helper implementation and call-site inventory.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Set versus WeakSet constant factors vary by engine, but lifetime and asymptotic work are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No unbounded retention or serialization-allocation regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review across all changed files. Submitted one low-severity repeated-work finding for per-turn launch-configuration rebuilding/YAML reparsing. Verified live setTools and prewarm changes generally remove SDK restarts, recorded the concrete URI-cache false-restart fix, and found no additional boundary, concurrency, cache-lifecycle, cleanup, or serialization regressions.
